newsitem.title: USA: Pioneer Natural Resources to sell at least $100 ml.
newsitem.headline: Pioneer Natural Resources to sell at least $100 ml.

text.p: Pioneer Natural Resources Co said it will sell at least $100 million of energy producing properties once the company is formed via the merger of MESA Inc and Parker & Parsley Petroleum Corp.
"We will sell $100-$200 million in properties to cut debt," said Jon Brumley chief executive of MESA and soon to be chief executive of Pioneer.
The merged company will inherit have $1.3 billion in debt, or 43 percent of book capital and plans to retain its investment grade rating.
"This is not a merger to cut costs but is for synergy," Brumley said.
He said that the Pioneer board, which includes the merged company's largest investor Richard Rainwater, would hold 17 percent of Pioneer's equity.
Scott Sheffield, chief exective of Parker & Parsley said that the company had identified another $10 million annual cost savings.

He said that the company, which will rank third in terms of U.S. independent energy producers, would expand its Spraberry field at 13-15 percent a year, adding 70 million barrels of oil equivalent to outut over seven years.

The combined company plans to spend $100 million on exploration this year out of a $300 million capital budget and said that it was looking at new operations in East Texas and Canada as well as a 200 million barrel of energy equivalent project in Venezuela.
It will also increase the capacity of its Hugoton Basin, western Kansas, gas processing plant by more than 50 percent, Brumley said.
